newsitem.title: INDIA: India Cochin up 10 pct near close.
newsitem.headline: India Cochin up 10 pct near close.

text.p: Shares of India's Cochin Refineries rose 13.50 rupees or nearly ten percent, to 149.25 at the Bombay exchange on Tuesday as traders expected the firm to benefit from an anticipated increase in government-set prices of petroleum products.
The shares were kept in check by exchange authorities as they reached the daily price limit of 10 percent. More than 89,100 shares were traded at the exchange near close of trade.
Higher prices for petroleum products will boost the state-run firm's income, traders said.

In a recent interview on state-run Doordarshan television, Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said he planned to raise oil prices to tackle the huge oil pool deficit -- pegged at 155 billion rupees ($4.32 million) by the end of 1996/97 (April-March).
The oil pool deficit is the subsidy the federal government owes to state-run oil companies for selling their products well below international prices.
